map: Lemma 4.1 pp.11–12: Taylor polynomial Gbar_x through degree p-1 has error <=L_p||y-x||^p/p! and derivative error <=L_p||y-x||^(p-1)/(p-1)!, without a continuous pth derivative.

Lemma 4.2 p.12: beta=2p L_p/p! regularization makes the known Taylor-model VI uniquely solvable; its dependence gives a measurable model operation. All model normals are genuine N_X normals independently of a distance promise.

Lemma 4.3 p.13: model normal n=-Gbar_x(y)-beta||y-x||^(p-1)(y-x) and evaluated G(y) give ||G(y)+n||<=A_p L_p a^p when ||x-zstar||<=a, A_p=(2p+1)3^p/p!. At most two queries include certificate evaluation.
Equations (4.4)–(4.6) p.13: lambda=1/(beta||y-x||^(p-1)), xplus=Pi_X(x-lambda G(y)), and 2lambda<G(y),y-u><=||x-u||^2-||xplus-u||^2-(3/4)||y-x||^2.

Proposition 4.5 p.14: summing the energy inequality and using convexity yields Lambda_T>= (3/4)^((p-1)/2)T^((p+1)/2)/(b_p L_p a^(p-1)), with b_p=2p/p!. The lambda-weighted feasible average has squared distance <=a^2/(2mu Lambda_T). T_p in (4.11) ensures Lambda_T>=2/mu and hence distance <=a/2. This is a distance guarantee, not a tangent-residual guarantee for the average.

Algorithm 2 p.15 repeats finite Halve schedules until A_p L_p a^p<=delta, then performs a model correction and checks its evaluated certificate. Equation (4.12) gives a scheduled cost <=C_p[1+(L_p R^(p-1)/mu)^(2/(p+1))+log_+(A_p L_p R^p/delta)]. This schedule bound holds even for invalid R; only distance success requires validity.

proofs.full_local_argument: Take the finite BaseTrial cost and valid-radius success established in Section 4 as the explicit premise of this reduction. Set rho=(mu/L_p)^(1/(p-1)) and use R_j=min(D,2^j rho), without repeating D, each from w. Since r<=D, there is a first valid guess, and its trial succeeds; earlier trials may also succeed, which only reduces cost. If rho>=D there is one guess, R=D, and kappa_D<=1. Otherwise, the largest executed guess is at most 2 max(r,rho): when r<=rho the first guess is already valid, and otherwise doubling crosses r by a factor at most two, possibly truncated at D. Therefore L_p R_j^(p-1)/mu<=2^(p-1)max(1,L_p r^(p-1)/mu) for all executed guesses. Their number is <=2+log_2(max(1,D/rho))=O_p(L_S), because D/rho=kappa_D^(1/(p-1)). Also R_j<=D, so log_+(A_p L_p R_j^p/delta)<=log_+(A_p L_p D^p/delta)=O_p(L_S). The Section 4 cost of each trial is thus <=C_p[1+(L_p r^(p-1)/mu)^(2/(p+1))]L_S. Summing O_p(L_S) trials proves the asserted bound. Finite schedules bound unsuccessful trials without assuming their radius promises. Genuine normals and evaluated final norm tests exclude false success. For r=0 the same inequalities give the additive bound. This completes the outer reduction conditional on the source-linked Section 4 base result.
map: Finite false-promise trial costs permit charging every unsuccessful radius.
The first valid geometric radius controls the distance-sensitive condition factor.
The number of guesses and each accuracy logarithm are bounded by L_S.

assumptions: Fixed integer p>=2; public L_p,D,mu,delta>0, dimension d>=1 and w in X.
G is C^(p-1) on an open neighborhood of X; ||D^(p-1)G(x)-D^(p-1)G(y)||_op<=L_p||x-y|| for x,y in X. No continuous pth derivative or separate lower-derivative bounds are assumed.
G is mu-strongly monotone on X: <G(x)-G(y),x-y>>=mu||x-y||^2.

Exact feasible order-p queries return (G,DG,...,D^(p-1)G). Exact projections and solutions of known regularized Taylor-model VIs are internal operations under Section 3.2. All original-operator queries, including certificate evaluations and nested descendants, are counted.

Use Algorithm 3 with Algorithm 2 BaseTrial, starting every trial from original w and accepting only a verified genuine normal certificate. Radius schedules remain finite on false promises; no artificial ball restriction changes X.
statement.conclusion: AdaptiveStrong(BaseTrial,G,w,mu,delta) returns (y,n,G(y)) with y in X, n in N_X(y), an already evaluated G(y), and ||G(y)+n||<=delta using at most C_p[1+(L_p r^(p-1)/mu)^(2/(p+1))]L_S(mu,delta)^2 original queries, equation (5.4) with gamma=2/(p+1), b=2. At r=0 use the additive constant convention; no zero-query claim follows.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Finite-dimensional Euclidean R^d; vector Euclidean norm and multilinear derivative operator norm. Known nonempty compact convex X with diam(X)<=D. N_X(x)={n:<n,u-x><=0 for all u in X}. G has unique VI solution zstar, characterized by -G(zstar) in N_X(zstar). r=||w-zstar|| is analysis-only. kappa_D=L_p D^(p-1)/mu and L_S(mu,delta)=1+log(2+kappa_D+L_p D^p/delta+mu D/delta). For comparison with Definition 5.1, Q_R=L_p R^p/epsilon and L_A(R,epsilon)=1+log(2+D/R+Q_R), 0<R<=D, epsilon>0. All log arguments are dimensionless.
statement.parameter_domains: p integer >=2; d>=1; L_p,D,mu,delta>0; w in X; 0<=r<=D. The constant depends on fixed p, not d, instance, accuracy or condition quantities.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every fixed p and every admissible public input and compatible G, there is a deterministic implementation with fixed known instance-independent leading constant C_p satisfying the conclusion. No initial distance r is supplied. No probability qualification is needed.
